## Learning Objectives

By the end of this chapter, you will be able to:

- Install Ibis and set up development environment
- Load and explore the World of Warcraft dataset
- Perform basic data exploration (shape, columns, sampling)
- Execute your first Ibis transformations

This chapter introduces Ibis and demonstrates basic data exploration using the World
of Warcraft avatar history dataset.

## Why Ibis Matters

Ibis provides a unified interface across different SQL dialects and data processing
frameworks. Instead of learning multiple syntaxes, you write Python code once and run
it on any backend.

## Working with the World of Warcraft Dataset

For this book, we'll use the World of Warcraft avatar history dataset, which contains
over 10 million records of auction house data. This dataset provides realistic complexity
for learning data analysis patterns while being manageable in size for local development.

```{python}
import ibis
from ibis import _

# Load World of Warcraft avatar history data
wowah = ibis.examples.wowah_data_raw.fetch()

# Basic exploration
print("Dataset shape:", wowah.count().execute(), "rows")
print("Columns:", wowah.columns)

# Sample data exploration
sample = wowah.head(3).execute()
print(sample)

# TODO: Add simple data analysis examples
```

This example shows the basic Ibis workflow: load data, explore its structure, and
perform simple transformations and filtering. The World of Warcraft dataset contains
auction house data with item names, quantities, server information, and other auction
details that we'll explore throughout this book.
